body.claim: A regular hexagonal grid has the least total wall of any way to divide a flat surface into equal-area cells.
body.why: This is the honeycomb theorem. It was first recorded in 36 BC by Varro, and in the 17th century Jan Brozek used a similar theorem to argue why bees create hexagonal honeycombs. It was finally proven in 1999 by Thomas Hales.

probes.question: Which grid uses the least total wall for cells of equal area?
True or false: the honeycomb conjecture was proven in 1999.
